prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by proteolysis-targeting chimeras, a design principle in which a bifunctional molecule induces proximity between a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged in substance: a single-part prize for the PROTAC core of B028, to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Round 1 showed that B028 is the only candidacy named in four preferred configurations (Aili, Aqvist, Linke and mine), and all eight members described its mechanism as confirmed, which is the evidence I weigh most. The chemistry is a physical principle I can state in mechanistic terms: a heterobifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity can be measured and tuned, the E3 ligase ubiquitinates the target, and the proteasome destroys it. Crews and Deshaies established the concept in 2001, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned it into a design discipline. That is a coherent three-name attribution on one achievement, and no earlier prize covers it. In response to the chair's question about maturity, I have narrowed the citation so that it recognises the mechanism and design principle and does not imply an approval count. I would not support a citation that reaches into the cereblon glue strand, because it would blur the attribution the three names rest on.
statement.case_against: Two objections remain and I do not think round 1 removed them. First, maturity: to my knowledge no degrader is yet an approved drug, so we would be rewarding a concept and its design rules ahead of the outcome, which is a position I hold with some discomfort. Second, attribution: the thalidomide-cereblon strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a distinct discovery that explained an existing drug's mechanism and arguably has the stronger clinical footprint. Choosing Ciulli over Handa for the third place is a judgment about which strand is the achievement, and I cannot settle it from the files. My criterion is that the chemistry which can be stated as a design rule, here the PROTAC, should be credited as the achievement, and the glue strand is better treated as a separate future case. A reader could still say this criterion is chosen to fit the three-name limit.

responses.point: Johan Aqvist asked what in the Gray and Winkler work is new in chemical terms compared with the 1992 Marcus prize, and stated that his own main reservation about B028 is clinical maturity.
responses.response: That question is fair and I cannot answer it well enough to carry B055. The new element is experimental: the distance and driving-force dependence of tunnelling through the protein matrix, measured on ruthenium-modified proteins. But that is the confirmation and extension of a recognised theory, and the committee would have to explain what a second prize adds. No other member has put it in a configuration, so I have dropped B055 from my alternatives and I have taken your maturity point on B028 seriously. I have narrowed the citation to the mechanism and design principle, so that the prize does not claim a therapeutic outcome. If you decide maturity alone rules out B028, I would like to know whether that would move you to B061 or to the older and clearly mature B008, because that decides whether B028 can reach five.

responses.point: Heiner Linke proposes a two-part prize, Liu for B061 and Crews and Deshaies for B028, which keeps the union at three people and gives two explainable chemical-biology stories.
responses.response: I see the logic, but I do not move to a two-part prize. Dropping Ciulli to make room for Liu changes the B028 attribution to one that would leave out the structure-based design rules that made PROTACs general. I find the Liu-only attribution of B061 hard to defend, since you yourself note that Komor and Gaudelli did the experimental work on the cytosine and adenine editors and that Kondo and Nishida reported a parallel approach. A prize that I expect to be challenged on attribution should not be the price of keeping the union at three. On your question of whether B061 and B028 can be compared on attribution clarity, novelty relative to prior prizes and maturity, I find B028 better on the first two and weaker on the third. I could support B061 as an alternative if the committee fixes its attribution in a way that the base-editing supporters agree on.

responses.point: Andrei Chabes argues that cytosine and adenine editing are separate chemical achievements and proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the sole prize, with a reservation about Kondo and Nishida.
responses.response: Your point that the adenine editor needed TadA to be evolved to act on DNA, with no natural counterpart, is chemically persuasive, and it is the best argument I have seen that B061 is more than a refinement of the 2020 prize. I still hesitate for the reasons you list yourself: a ten-year-old field with a short clinical record and a parallel invention that a three-name prize leaves out. Compared with B028 I rate base editing as stronger on chemical novelty of the deamination step and weaker on attribution, because the credit would sit with the lead investigator and his two trainees while Kondo and Nishida are excluded. I keep B061 as my first alternative, and if the committee cannot reach five on B028 I would be willing to look at your three-name configuration.

responses.point: Peter Somfai argues that B008 is the cleanest case on the table for chemistry at its core and that B008 should stand alone as a two-laureate prize if B061 does not carry.
responses.response: I accept that B008 has the strongest evidence on attribution and maturity: the independent development by Buchwald and Hartwig, thirty years of use and no maturity concern. This is where my first-round position was too narrow, since I did not list it as an alternative at all. My remaining question is the one you raise yourself, namely whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize leaves room for amination. I would want the expert report to say what the ligand design and the difficult C-N reductive elimination add mechanistically, as opposed to the earlier C-C chemistry. For this round I add B008 as an alternative in place of B055, and I would not oppose it as a stand-alone prize if B028 fails on maturity.

responses.point: Daniel Aili stresses that the PROTAC principle is a molecular design in the strict sense, with ligand and linker choice and ternary-complex cooperativity all tunable, and that Handa could be weighed against Ciulli.
responses.response: I agree with the design framing and have used it in the citation. On the Handa question, the criterion I would apply is whether the credited work is a design principle that can be learned and repeated, and the cereblon story is closer to a mechanistic explanation of a drug already in use. This is a strong discovery, but a different one, and I prefer to keep the PROTAC citation specific so that the glue strand can be assessed separately. If the committee decides otherwise I would prefer to see a separate part for glues than a swap of Handa for Ciulli, but that cannot fit within three names, so I treat it as a reason for the committee to reconsider the configuration and not as a change in mine.

uncertainties: Whether degrader clinical validation is mature enough, given that I know of no approved PROTAC drug.
Whether Ciulli or Handa should hold the third place, which I judge on the design-rule criterion but which the expert reports should settle.
Whether the committee will accept a citation limited to the PROTAC mechanism while the cereblon glue strand is left unrecognised.
Whether the 2010 prize leaves enough room for B008, which I have not evaluated myself because it is outside my field.
Whether B028 can reach five votes without the members who place maturity first, since only four of us named it in round 1.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict applies to B028 or to the alternatives B061 and B008. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou; B008 is her preferred candidacy but I have no tie to Buchwald or Hartwig, and she does not work on any candidacy in my configuration. My field, proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes, is close to B055, which I have now dropped as an alternative, and I recorded that overlap as a possible bias in round 1. No recusal is requested.
